newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR SOFTER UNDER IMPORT PRESSURE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR SOFTER UNDER IMPORT PRESSURE.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar was quoted easier on the key U.S. dollar on Wednesday morning on the back of a rise in importer demand for that currency, foreign exchange dealers said.
"There is increased demand (for U.S. dollars) and we expect a slight depreciation in the local dollar today," a dealer said, adding:
"It doesn't look like the central bank will intervene (to bail out the local unit)."
The dealer said most banks could be stocking up in advance for a big import payment coming up next week.
"We're likely to see rates continue going up because of that," he said.

At around 0820 GMT the Zimbabwe dollar was trading weaker at 11.3775/3875 on the U.S. unit after finishing at 11.3700/3800 the previous day and was also softer at 19.0615/0815 from 18.9600/9900 versus pound sterling.
It was at 6.3495/3595 from 6.3200/3400 against the mark and at 2.4970/5020 to the rand from 2.4900/5100.
